Could a proposed decihertz space interferometer measure cosmic acceleration directly through long-duration neutron-star inspiral phases, supplying information needed to break the luminosity-distance degeneracy with spatial curvature?
Why is vacuum energy so small, can dynamical dark energy reduce fine tuning or cosmic coincidence, and how can observations distinguish a cosmological constant from evolving quintessence?

Does two-field slow-roll inflation retain an observable tensor–scalar consistency condition after model-dependent super-horizon evolution and reheating, and can late-time correlations reconstruct the curvature spectrum at horizon exit?

How accurately can precision distance–redshift observations reconstruct recent cosmic expansion, locate the acceleration–deceleration transition, constrain evolving dark energy, and test alternative explanations of acceleration?

Can Planck-scale corrections to a natural-inflation potential generate oscillating or scale-dependent primordial spectra, and could their signatures survive transfer into CMB temperature, polarization, and matter spectra?

Can atmospheric dispersion, evolving isotopic abundances, or errors associated with particular transitions explain the absorption-line shifts previously interpreted as a smaller fine-structure constant at high redshift?

What are the leading non-Gaussian scalar and tensor three-point functions in single-field inflation, including their numerical coefficients, momentum dependence and squeezed limits? How are these calculations related to cosmological wavefunctions and hypothetical dS/CFT correlators?

Can negative-kinetic-energy scalar models realize dark energy with w<−1 while avoiding catastrophic decay over a cosmological lifetime, particularly when regarded as effective theories with a momentum cutoff?

What is the simplest model fitting first-year WMAP TT and TE spectra, does its WMAP-only fit predict other astronomical observations, and what constraints follow when external data and additional cosmological parameters are included?

What do first-year WMAP temperature and polarization observations imply about superhorizon initial fluctuations, single-field inflation, correlated CDM isocurvature, and possible features in the inflaton potential?

Can spatial fluctuations in inflaton decay couplings generate the dominant primordial density perturbations through inhomogeneous reheating, and how would this change inflationary scale, spectral-tilt and non-Gaussianity predictions?
Can inflationary fluctuations of light moduli generate observable relic and curvature perturbations through early spatial variations of couplings, even after those couplings become homogeneous?

What can semiclassical gravity and self-consistent measurement theory say about a hypothetical finite-state quantum theory of de Sitter space, its observables, mathematical ambiguities and flat-space limit? The paper summarizes two lectures and presents an exploratory toy model.

How can inflationary light-field fluctuations generate superhorizon metric perturbations through spatially varying reheating, freeze-out and temporary particle domination, and what non-Gaussianity follows from this conversion?
Do relative shifts of QSO absorption transitions indicate variation of the fine-structure constant, and can instrumental or astrophysical systematic effects explain those shifts?
Can a residual de Sitter α-vacuum produce observable ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays today, what bound follows on its vacuum parameter, and could saturation explain super-GZK events?

What constraint on varying fundamental couplings follows from comparing meteoritic ¹⁸⁷Re decay with present laboratory measurements, once the interpretation of the meteoritic precision and the decay rate's time average is corrected?
Can a scalar with order-unity matter couplings evade terrestrial gravity tests through environmental screening while producing detectable fifth forces or equivalence-principle violations in space?
Can an environmentally dependent scalar mass allow gravitational-strength matter couplings while suppressing terrestrial fifth forces and retaining observable effects in space?

What information about the dark-energy equation of state w(z) can varying-α observations recover when the scalar–electromagnetic coupling is specified, and what measurement precision would be required?

Can an independently analyzed, homogeneous set of high-quality quasar absorption spectra constrain cosmological variation of α, while simulations guide selection against weak-line and velocity-blending systematics?

What limit on cosmological variation of low-energy α follows from a new many-multiplet analysis using an independent fitting code and a uniform, high-quality quasar absorption sample, with simulation-based controls on blending and weak lines?

How low can the reheating temperature be when light-element abundances are combined with CMB and large-scale-structure constraints, including a direct decay channel from the reheating particle into neutrinos?

Can a holographically constrained vacuum energy with a cosmological infrared cutoff describe a variable, true cosmological constant while respecting gravitational conservation identities and the observational requirements discussed in the paper?

How much does a stellar-population lower bound on cosmic age tighten supernova constraints on a varying dark-energy equation of state, and what dynamical models could accommodate the suggested evolution across W = −1?
In positive-density, single-scalar dark-energy models with w < -1, must fluctuations about a homogeneous background have negative gradient energy, and does this determine the time-kinetic sign?

Can interacting quintessence and multiple dark-matter components explain an apparent supernova equation of state below -1, delay acceleration until after a substantial matter era, and produce comparable future dark-sector densities without a Big Rip?

Can a scalar with ordinary kinetic sign, exponential potential, and nonminimal gravitational coupling have stable expanding solutions that pass through w < -1 and approach de Sitter space for large sets of initial conditions?
How well can future CMB–galaxy correlations constrain the physical scale and amplitude of dark-energy clustering, and thereby test canonical single-scalar quintessence?

Does the low-redshift galaxy correlation function contain the predicted baryon acoustic peak, and can its acoustic and equality scales constrain cosmological distances, matter density, dark energy and spatial curvature?

Can simple canonical quintessence models be classified by their equation-of-state dynamics, and what observational precision and microphysical restrictions could distinguish them from one another or from a cosmological constant?
Can NEC-violating inflation with increasing H support classically stable cosmological perturbations, and how would its scalar and tensor predictions differ from conventional inflation?

Can several uncoupled quintessence fields improve dark-energy phenomenology through assisted evolution, particularly for exponential and inverse-power potentials, and can their joint background dynamics be represented by an equivalent single-field potential?

Can a conventional quintessence field climbing its potential reproduce supernova distances interpreted as constant-w dark energy with w < −1, while avoiding phantom kinetic terms? Which observations could distinguish this mechanism?

Under what solar-system, pulsar-timing and gravitational-constant-variation constraints can scalar-tensor gravity yield an effective present dark-energy equation of state significantly below −1? Conversely, how could a robust measurement of w0 constrain departures from GR?

Can interaction between canonical quintessence and dark matter generate an inferred dark-energy equation of state below −1 when observations are analyzed assuming noninteracting CDM, and what distance, matter-density and structure-growth signatures could reveal the interaction?
Can extended global symmetries and associated flat directions in one supersymmetric model jointly account for baryon asymmetry, asymmetric dark matter and axion-like dark energy?

Can interactions between super-Hubble scalar perturbations and an environment of shorter-wavelength modes suppress quantum coherence during inflation, and is gravitational backreaction sufficient within 60 e-foldings?

Which properties of short-wavelength environments allow primordial long-wavelength quantum fluctuations to become a classical stochastic field ensemble, and can decoherence finish between horizon exit and re-entry even for gravitational-strength interactions?

Can a phenomenological modification of gravity inspired by the Chaplygin density law accommodate chaotic inflation, and which Chaplygin and inflaton scales satisfy the paper's CMB constraints? The authors aim to identify required assumptions and extrapolations rather than establish superiority over conventional inflation.
Can a wide-field galaxy redshift survey test dark-energy smoothness through the three-dimensional galaxy power spectrum, and separate its scale dependence from massive-neutrino effects?
Do the published VLT/UVES null constraints on varying α faithfully represent their spectra and absorption-profile models, and what results follow after correcting the parameter-estimation procedure?
Does the historical HiRes ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray spectrum exhibit a statistically significant suppression consistent with the predicted GZK cutoff, and where are the cutoff and ankle?

Does describing inflationary perturbations as squeezed quantum states produce physical predictions absent from standard treatments, and do spectral oscillations or desqueezing demonstrate observable quantum coherence?

Can coupled scalar fields produce inflationary regimes and endings beyond gradual slow rollover and first-order bubble transitions? The paper develops a rapid waterfall model and Brans–Dicke hybrids with curvature-induced or slow-roll symmetry breaking.

Can two-field false-vacuum inflation in Einstein gravity produce viable perturbations and a successful end to inflation, and can its potential arise naturally in supersymmetry or string-derived supergravity? The paper emphasizes vacuum domination and second-order transitions, while also treating first-order bubble nucleation.
Can primordial monopole interiors inflate, survive the end of inflation outside, and seed eternal self-reproduction despite conventional estimates based on small vacuum monopole sizes?

How can potential-based and Hubble-based slow-roll approximations be defined consistently, extended order by order, and used to describe inflationary dynamics and its endpoint while retaining the necessary attractor conditions?

Can a technically natural ultralight pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson supply a temporary homogeneous energy component at recent epochs, reconcile low clustered matter density with spatial flatness, and increase the expansion age while respecting the paper's gravitational-lensing constraints?

What analytic expressions determine the curvature-perturbation spectrum and spectral index when inflation has several real dynamical scalar degrees of freedom, including a curved scalar-field space, rather than the single degree assumed in the standard calculation?

Can a first-order transition sustain inflation with an approximately equilibrated thermal component, sufficient density perturbations and many e-folds, without a tiny coupling or a separate large reheating episode?

Can simple inflationary models generate strongly blue, non-Gaussian entropy perturbations, suppressing horizon-scale microwave anisotropy relative to galaxy-scale structure, and under what decay histories do these become adiabatic perturbations?

Can a dynamical negative-pressure component replace Λ in flat, low-matter-density cosmologies, and can its fluctuations and equation-of-state history be distinguished through CMB anisotropy and the mass power spectrum?

Can a primordial, persistently subdominant exponential scalar field improve SCDM structure formation without introducing a scalar energy scale characteristic of recent epochs, while satisfying early-universe and historical observational constraints?

Can relative wavelength shifts between light- and heavy-element absorption lines improve sensitivity to cosmological variation of α, and does the observed MgII/FeII sample require such variation after statistical and systematic uncertainties?

Can multiple scalar fields with individually steep exponential potentials cooperate through cosmic expansion to produce inflation, and what scaling attractor and curvature-perturbation spectrum result when their slopes differ?

Can nearby and distant Type Ia supernova luminosity distances constrain matter density, a cosmological constant, current acceleration, the expansion's fate, and cosmic age, while surviving plausible observational systematics?
Can a symmetry suppress observable couplings between a nearly massless quintessence field and ordinary matter while retaining a detectable electromagnetic polarization-rotation signal?

Can scalar-field tracker evolution reduce the initial-condition tuning behind present-day matter–quintessence coincidence, produce late acceleration, and predict a relation between present matter density and quintessence equation of state?

Which scalar potentials admit exact power-law scaling of scalar energy density during perfect-fluid domination, when are these solutions attractors, and can their evolution help explain late scalar domination?

How low can the reheating temperature after late decay of massive particles be while remaining compatible with BBN, once incomplete neutrino thermalization is calculated explicitly? What additional signatures arise in large-scale structure and CMB anisotropies?

What constraints on matter density and cosmological-constant density follow from the Type Ia supernova magnitude–redshift relation, and how robust are they to selection, extinction, calibration, and supernova evolution?

Why is the assisted-inflation scaling trajectory an attractor for many exponential-potential fields, and what homogeneous, adiabatic, and isocurvature perturbations arise near it without a slow-roll approximation?

Which scalar potentials admit tracker solutions insensitive to initial conditions, what relation do they impose between present quintessence density and equation of state, and can they make late quintessence domination more plausible?

Which spatially flat matter-plus-quintessence models satisfy the paper's historical cosmological observations, how do conservative concordance bounds differ from Gaussian likelihood bounds, and which observations could distinguish quintessence from Λ?

Can general nonminimal scalar–gravity couplings produce scaling attractors with appreciable scalar energy and present acceleration, with dynamics determined by the relation between coupling and potential rather than their individual functional forms?

How do cross-couplings and repeated appearances of scalar fields in multiple exponential potential terms modify assisted power-law inflation, and under what conditions do the generalized potentials admit scaling solutions?

Can an anisotropy-driven relativistic two-stream instability generate the magnetic fields required in internal GRB shocks and external afterglow shocks, and can polarization scintillations test this mechanism?

Can one non-minimally coupled scalar provide present quintessence and a varying gravitational coupling while satisfying local gravity bounds, and what signatures does this produce in linear CMB and matter perturbations?
Which accelerated cosmological trajectories exist for a scalar with an exponential potential and explicit linear matter coupling, and how do their CMB and matter perturbations constrain the coupling?

Does anthropic selection explain a small effective vacuum energy and the coincidence of galaxy formation with vacuum domination when the prior is derived from a specific cosmological model rather than assumed flat?

Can a positive-density dark component with w < −1 produce a workable classical cosmology and satisfy the observational tests considered in the paper, and how would its background and perturbations differ from conventional dark energy?

Can energy exchange between an exponential-potential scalar field and matter change cosmological attractors, permit inflation without eliminating matter, and produce oscillatory approach to late-time solutions relevant to inflation or accelerated expansion?

Can sums of exponential scalar potentials combine early radiation/matter scaling with late quintessence domination, yielding a sufficiently negative present equation of state over a wide range of initial conditions?

How does an initially stable, nearly pure 85Rb condensate respond when its scattering length is suddenly made sufficiently negative to trigger collapse, and how do loss, bursts, jets, and surviving remnants depend on interaction strength and initial conditions?

Which symmetry conditions ensure topological quantum order (TQO), understood as robustness against quasi-local perturbations, at zero and finite temperature? Which commonly associated diagnostics are insufficient?
Does an infinite-range random quantum Heisenberg magnet support a quantum-disordered spin-fluid ground state, and what is its low-frequency local spin response?

Which parallel, transverse, or oblique instability grows fastest in a relativistic electron beam–plasma system, how does this hierarchy depend on density, drift energy, and temperature, and how does multidimensional nonlinear evolution modify it?

Can scalar perturbations of a scalar-field FRW background be reduced to an unconstrained variable with conventional kinetic signature, making the false-vacuum bounce negative mode explicit while remaining consistent with the earlier no-negative-mode theorem?
How reliable are energy conditions as hypotheses for singularity, positive-mass and censorship theorems when quantum fields and apparently reasonable classical scalar fields violate them?
How does nonminimal scalar–curvature coupling change cosmic acceleration for a given potential, and when are slow-roll approximations and conformal transformation methods justified?
Does gravitational false-vacuum decay possess the negative fluctuation mode needed for a decay interpretation, and why do different reductions to one physical variable give different answers?

Do cosmic-string cusps generate individually distinguishable gravitational-wave bursts, what are their waveform and amplitude–rate relations, and could the then-planned LIGO/VIRGO and LISA detectors observe them?
Do Page’s confined-field counterexamples, low-temperature states, and proliferation-of-species argument violate S ≤ 2πER when E includes the gravitating energy of every essential system component?

What critical points and expansion histories occur in FRW universes containing dust and a negative-pressure component with constant equation of state, and how well can background observations distinguish constant from varying equations of state?

What waveforms, amplitudes, beaming patterns, and occurrence rates arise from cosmic-string cusps and kinks, and how does their non-Gaussian burst population alter detector prospects and pulsar-timing constraints?

Can a dilaton running toward infinite bare coupling supply late-time quintessence, satisfy visible-matter gravity constraints, and sustain accelerated expansion with a finite dark-energy/dark-matter ratio?

Can higher-order curvature terms supply effective negative pressure and accelerated cosmological expansion without introducing a separate minimally coupled quintessence field? Which f(R) choices admit exact examples, and how do their Jordan- and Einstein-frame descriptions connect?

How can cosmological event horizons be located using proper-distance light-ray diagrams and kinematics rather than an explicit matter dynamics? When does accelerated expansion admit no horizon, and how does the proposed asymptotic horizon relate to an actual event horizon?

Can cosmological attraction toward infinite bare string coupling suppress a massless dilaton's interactions while leaving observable violations of free-fall universality or variations of constants, quantitatively related to inflationary density fluctuations?

How did the cosmological term evolve from Einstein's 1917 construction into a quantum vacuum-energy problem, and which historical motivations, observational episodes and early quantum arguments shaped that transition?
Does supporting a traversable wormhole require a large total quantity of energy-condition-violating matter, or can a suitable quantitative measure become arbitrarily small?
Can the holographic bound on vacuum fluctuation entropy explain the small positive cosmological constant through Zel’dovich’s relation, and why should its mass scale be the QCD transition scale?

Can the zero-cosmological-constant holostar be interpreted as densely packed radial strings bounded by a membrane, providing both a black-hole alternative and a cosmological model with string-like cold dark matter?

Which features of scalar–tensor gravity are constrained by solar-system experiments, compact binaries and cosmology, and when must local and cosmological observations be combined to discriminate between theories?

Which higher-dimensional eternal black holes admit single-asymptotic-region geon quotients carrying gauge charge or angular momentum, and what restrictions follow from dimension, orientability and gauge-bundle topology?

Can interactions between long and short wavelength sectors of the inflaton suppress quantum coherences during inflation, and how do the resulting stochastic forces affect subsequent dynamics and selected fluctuation spectra?

How should a slicing-invariant volume for stationary black holes extend to two-dimensional dilaton gravity, and can a black hole have infinite volume while retaining finite area without pathological global structure?
Review how experiments test GR, distinguish alternative gravitational theories, and constrain new interactions, from equivalence-principle tests through post-Newtonian and compact-object gravity.

What restrictions do real electromagnetic fields and causal response impose on quantum-gravity-inspired electrodynamics, its constitutive relations, helicity-dependent refraction indices, and absorption?
How many homogeneous negative fluctuation modes surround gravitational oscillating bounces, and what does that count imply for their proposed contribution to false-vacuum tunnelling?

Which critical-point cosmologies exist for multiple exponential potentials, and when are they attractors against scalar, fluid and spatial-curvature perturbations? How does cross-coupling change the assisting behavior of independent fields?

How should interferometer searches detect cosmic-string cusp bursts, estimate realistic event rates for arbitrary loop distributions, and translate a nondetection into model-dependent parameter constraints?

How can a broad class of quantum-gravity-motivated corrections to classical electrodynamics be described phenomenologically, and what do they imply for electromagnetic propagation, energy transport, birefringence, and cutoff-related causality?

Does quantum information theory impose a temperature-dependent minimum relaxation time for perturbed thermodynamic systems, and do black-hole quasinormal resonances comply with or saturate that bound?

Can horizon-scale quantum fluctuations, particularly those generated by the trace anomaly, dynamically screen cosmological vacuum energy without ultraviolet fine tuning, and yield observable conformal signatures in the CMB?
Can matter with sound or signal speeds exceeding c form a physically acceptable relativistic theory, even when its macroscopic equations are covariant and arise from a Lorentz-invariant Lagrangian?
Can a nonflat vacuum gravitational instanton exist on R^3 × S^1 with asymptotically flat noncompact directions and a fixed Euclidean period only near infinity?

Within a two-geometry gravitational framework, how generally may the physical geometry governing matter differ from the gravitational metric? Can a Finsler physical geometry satisfy weak equivalence, causality, and consistency between particle and field descriptions?

What is the average von Neumann entropy of the smaller subsystem of a bipartite quantum system in a random pure state, and how much information remains accessible within that subsystem rather than in correlations?

Can observers actively probe nontrivial spacetime topology using causal signals arriving from past null infinity and returning to future null infinity? The paper seeks sufficient causal and energy hypotheses forbidding such probes.

Can self-reproducing chaotic inflation approach a stationary statistical description, despite continuing expansion and nonstationary comoving fields? The paper distinguishes recurring local domain properties from global stationarity of probability distributions.
Does accounting for Unruh–Wald buoyancy preserve a GSL-based entropy bound, and can species proliferation, additional spatial dimensions, or information-storing black hole remnants evade it?

In general Lagrangian gravity, can the first-law horizon term be written as κ/(2π) times the variation of a local geometrical entropy, and how does that entropy relate to Noether charge, dynamical horizons and Euclidean methods?

What restrictions do unitary black hole physics and entropy counting place on microscopic quantum-gravity degrees of freedom, and can local discrete models realize the resulting surface encoding while retaining nontrivial dynamics and the required symmetries?
Which conditions on a scalar-dependent Gauss–Bonnet coupling ensure the existence of classical singularity-free solutions in spatially flat FRW cosmology?

Do distinct quantum-gravity arguments suggest a fundamental limit to position and time resolution, and what would such a limit imply for ultraviolet behavior, measurement, causality and classical spacetime?

What information accounts for black hole entropy, and can the same quantum fluctuations explain both horizon entanglement and the gravitational coupling appearing in A/(4ħG), including its dependence on matter species?

Can a hyperbolic four-manifold with totally geodesic initial and final boundaries of different topology provide an explicit semiclassical topology-changing tunneling geometry in four-dimensional gravity with negative cosmological constant?

Can one explicitly construct hyperbolic four-manifolds with topologically different, totally geodesic initial and final spatial boundaries, and estimate their topology-changing tunneling amplitudes in quantum cosmology?

How do vacuum-generated cosmological perturbations acquire semiclassical stochastic behavior and effective decoherence, and how do the Heisenberg mode-function and Schrödinger squeezed-state descriptions express the same predictions?
Can nonperturbative gravity with a finite spatial boundary yield Chern–Simons boundary observables and state spaces, and conditionally realize holography and an area bound on information?

Can asymptotically anti-de Sitter wormholes admit a finite, gauge-invariant Euclidean variational principle and a quantum Hilbert space whose physical states are superpositions of wormhole wave functions?
What Lorentzian spacetimes correspond semiclassically to Λ=0 topological states supported on flat SL(2,C) connections, and which connection moduli admit physically acceptable geometries?
Does the Giddings–Strominger Euclidean wormhole possess a negative fluctuation mode, and does this support an imaginary semiclassical contribution interpreted as emission of baby universes?

Can longitudinal time dependence remove the singularity of an isolated gravitating global string while preserving a fixed proper core width, and what expansion rate and exterior geometry would result?

What instantons and semiclassical rates describe neutral and magnetically charged black-hole pair creation during inflation, how do the holes evolve, and what relic abundance follows within the adopted inflationary model?
Can black-hole formation and evaporation admit a unitary scattering matrix with finite entropy and a discrete spectrum, and what horizon degrees of freedom would implement it?

Which charged Nariai geometries survive in Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton theories, how do their solution spaces depend on the dilaton couplings and potential, and under what background conditions could their instantons describe black-hole pair creation?

Does the Giddings–Strominger Euclidean wormhole contribute a real or imaginary term to the forward flat-space amplitude, and can baby-universe emission produce loss of coherence in the parent subsystem?

How can cosmological perturbation back reaction be described by a gauge-independent effective energy-momentum tensor using spatial averaging at each time, including frozen wavelengths beyond the horizon?

Can dilatonic Charged Nariai instantons mediate black-hole pair creation during extended chaotic inflation, and how do their Lorentzian evolution, creation probabilities and allowed charges differ from standard inflation?
Construct U-duality solution-generating transformations for dilaton–axion gravity with multiple vector fields, and classify nonrotating black-hole geometries and BPS limits by charge alignment.

Can asymptotic gravitational energy and the stated little subgroup of Poincaré symmetry be quantized in the real connection representation, with a well-defined positive energy operator and an anomaly-free symmetry algebra under suitable quantum boundary conditions?

Which black-hole spacetimes arise from discrete AdS3 identifications with time-symmetric initial data and one asymptotic region, and how do interior topology, horizon formation, trapped curves and topological censorship behave?

These lectures review how quantum fields are interpreted on curved backgrounds, how gravitational fields create particles, how stress tensors are renormalized, what constrains negative energy, and where semiclassical gravity requires a fluctuating-metric description.

Can the growth of the number of spacetime topologies explain a small cosmological constant through a thermodynamic interpretation of the Euclidean gravitational path integral, with added excitation producing topology rather than increasing |Λ|?

Does gravitational collapse from nonsingular, asymptotically flat initial data generically keep singularities and their effects inaccessible to distant observers? This review addresses weak cosmic censorship, rather than strong cosmic censorship.

Which spacetime topologies dominate the four-dimensional Euclidean gravitational path integral for each sign of Λ, and can topology multiplicity overwhelm action suppression? The paper explores implications for spacetime foam, the cosmological constant, and the Hartle–Hawking wave function.

What are the late-time attractors of a universe containing a barotropic fluid and a scalar with an exponential potential, including potentials too steep to drive inflation? What relic scalar abundance follows at nucleosynthesis, and can a separate period of inflation suppress it?
What elementary cobordisms generate topology change in three dimensions, and how might this decomposition organize the sum over topologies in quantum gravity?

How can inflationary perturbations of quantum origin acquire classical stochastic behavior without changing the scenario's quantitative predictions, and what distinct roles do squeezing and environmental decoherence play?

Is the scalar quadratic Euclidean action about a Hawking–Turok singular instanton non-negative, and can its homogeneous perturbation sector contain negative modes for particular scalar potentials and instanton initial data?

At what symmetry-breaking scales do gauge and global string cores inflate in 3+1 dimensions, how do winding and coupling affect onset, and can time-dependent evolution avoid the exterior curvature singularities of static descriptions?

Can a scalar field coupled to the quadratic Gauss–Bonnet invariant support nonsingular open and closed FRW cosmologies, and can the singular families be confined to only part of the classical phase space?

What minimum energy-condition violations are required for an FRW universe to pass from contraction through a positive-size minimum into expansion, and can ordinary classical matter models support such a bounce?

Can tracing out bosonic perturbations produce a finite, physically consistent reduced inflaton density matrix and quantify the emergence of classical behavior near inflation's onset, including its dependence on environmental field variables?
Which scalar–fluid scaling solutions remain stable when spatial curvature is admitted, and what determines the past and future asymptotic states of expanding Robertson–Walker models?

Does the regular Coleman–De Luccia bounce with minimum Euclidean action have a monotonic tunneling field and no negative fluctuation modes, thereby resolving the proposed negative-mode criterion for gravitational false-vacuum decay?
How does nonminimal scalar–curvature coupling affect the existence, equation of state, and stability of cosmological scaling solutions for inverse power-law and exponential scalar potentials?

How should semiclassical Wheeler–De Witt branches be interpreted without an external time, and when is a Born–Oppenheimer-type treatment of matter stable in classically forbidden scale-factor regions?

Which Morse topology changes admit causally continuous histories, and can Morse indices provide a selection rule for the gravitational sum over histories? The paper addresses a weaker version of the Borde–Sorkin conjecture; the proposed connection to finite quantum-field propagation is a separate conjecture.

Can a dedicated accelerator search detect light particles with very small fractional electric charge through rare excitation and ionization, or exclude a conditional region of their charge–mass parameter space?

How accurately do free bosonic and Nambu–Goto effective strings describe confining SU(2) Polyakov-loop correlations at low and intermediate temperatures, and do comparisons with SU(3) and Ising gauge theories suggest universality beyond the free-string limit?
What laboratory, cosmological and stellar observations constrain the mass and electric charge of millicharged fermions, and how do the bounds depend on a paraphoton or a neutrino interpretation?
Can nonabelian discrete gauge symmetries protect a slow-roll inflaton potential against gravitational-strength corrections while also supplying special field values at which hybrid inflation ends?

Can explicit low-energy supergravity models use nonabelian discrete gauge symmetries to protect inflaton flatness, provide viable hybrid or mutated-hybrid exits, and permit unusually low inflationary energy scales?
Can a terrestrial detector observe solar Kaluza–Klein (KK) axions through coincident two-photon decays, and what coupling sensitivity and existing limits follow in low-scale quantum-gravity models?

How can extra dimensions lower the fundamental gravitational scale, and how must neutrino masses, Standard Model extensions, gauge unification and proton stability be reconsidered in that setting? These are introductory lectures reviewing proposals available in 2000.

Can cosmological background matter prevent heterotic dilaton/modulus overshoot, and do direct moduli–matter couplings improve stabilization? The paper studies both gravitational background damping and the extra forces induced by matter-dependent kinetic and potential terms.

Can a small spontaneously broken discrete gauged flavor symmetry accommodate charged-fermion hierarchies, large atmospheric neutrino mixing and either historical solar MSW solution, while controlling supersymmetric flavor-changing neutral currents?
Can intersecting D-branes provide a phenomenological origin for chiral quarks and leptons, family replication and hierarchical couplings, while supporting a low string scale and proton stability?

Does efficient nonthermal fermion production after inflation produce dangerous late-time gravitinos, or predominantly inflatinos, when inflation and vacuum supersymmetry breaking belong to separate sectors?

If proton-decay interactions are forbidden while ΔB = 2 operators survive, can strangeness-changing two-nucleon decays probe a low quantum-gravity scale, and how does the inferred sensitivity depend on hadronic clustering and flavor suppression?

Can small-field inflation with a leading quadratic field dependence generate acceptable scalar perturbations at electroweak or lower energy scales, with viable initial conditions and controlled termination?

Can extra-dimensional locality produce an accidental anomalous global Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected by a gauged U(1), while accommodating DFSZ or hadronic axions and correlated supersymmetry/PQ breaking scales?

Can an infinite spectrum with modular-invariance-induced cancellations stabilize the electroweak scale and address the cosmological constant without spacetime supersymmetry or an extra-dimensional hierarchy mechanism? The paper proposes a perspective, explicitly not a complete solution or realistic model.
Can a second scalar terminate tracker quintessence, avoiding an eternally accelerating future, and can the required potential and tiny energy density arise from brane interactions?

Can spontaneous CP breaking generate an order-one CKM phase through radiative effects while supersymmetric non-renormalization protects the strong CP phase, and can that protection survive realistic supersymmetry breaking?

How can scalar matter and gravitational perturbations be calculated accurately to first order in slow roll for arbitrarily many fields with nonminimal kinetic terms, including horizon crossing, trajectory rotation and entropy sourcing?

Can the primordial large-scale curvature perturbation originate from a light field unrelated to the fields driving inflation, through its later oscillation and decay, and what conditions control its spectrum, Gaussianity and residual isocurvature?
How does a primordial fluctuation of a modulus that later dominates and decays affect the CMB, the inference of inflationary parameters, and possible correlated baryon isocurvature signatures?
Can electroweak-scale gauged Lμ−Lτ explain the possible positive muon anomalous-moment discrepancy, accommodate nearly bimaximal neutrino mixing, and yield observable collider signatures?

Can a cosmic scalar produce the historically suggested fractional change δα/α≈10−4 without radiatively generating a vacuum-energy variation incompatible with standard cosmology or requiring extraordinary fine tuning?

Can a dynamical bulk three-form provide an adjustable integration constant supporting flat four-dimensional slices in an RS-II model without retuning the brane tension, and can its scalar dual have a Goldstone-boson interpretation?

Can a Wilson-line PNGB remain ultralight despite Planck-scale global-symmetry breaking and provide a natural axion or quintessence field, potentially with its tiny potential generated by Planck effects themselves?

How do correlated variations of gauge and Yukawa couplings, Λ_QCD and quark masses alter nuclear limits on fine-structure variation from Oklo, long-lived radioactive isotopes and stellar bound-state β-decays?
How can inflation address the horizon, flatness and entropy problems while generating quantum perturbations that seed cosmic structure, CMB anisotropies and gravitational waves?
How do supersymmetric axion partners change cosmological bounds on the QCD axion decay constant, and when do generic light pseudoscalar moduli create additional cosmological problems?
Can a discrete gauge symmetry simultaneously protect MSSM R parity, forbid a bare μ term while allowing Giudice–Masiero generation, and explain fermion mass and mixing hierarchies?

Can six-dimensional universal extra dimension models with a low fundamental scale simultaneously explain small neutrino masses and suppress nucleon decay, while providing viable Kaluza–Klein dark matter candidates?

Can discrete gauge remnants protect the Peccei–Quinn axion against Planck-suppressed symmetry violation, while realizing DFSZ and KSVZ models and linking the axion scale to supersymmetry breaking and the μ term?

Can nonanomalous discrete R symmetries generate µ ≃ 1 TeV from fractional powers of the superpotential VEV when the gravitino is lighter than the weak scale, while sufficiently suppressing baryon- and lepton-number violation?

Does inverse nuclear bremsstrahlung reabsorb gravitationally trapped KK gravitons quickly enough to invalidate neutron-star gamma-ray or heating bounds, and how do supernova and neutron-star bounds scale with the number of large extra dimensions?

Can a discrete gauge symmetry protect nucleons against baryon-number violation when the new-physics cutoff is low, while allowing small neutrino masses, and can that symmetry arise from an economical anomaly-free continuous gauge theory?
How does the microscopic origin of photon mass affect bounds inferred from galactic vector potentials, and when can Higgs vortices make a massive photon behave effectively Maxwellian on large scales?

Which theoretical possibilities motivate experimentally accessible violations of the gravitational inverse-square law, what do short-range and astronomical experiments constrain, and how could a detected violation be characterized?

How do millicharged particles coupled to baryons at recombination alter CMB anisotropy, and how tightly can historical WMAP data combined with a BBN baryon prior constrain their abundance and remaining mass-charge window?
How low must the ultraviolet cutoff of a scalar ghost effective theory be to suppress observable vacuum instability, and can a Lorentz-invariant cutoff suffice?

Can classical Einstein gravity and the closed trapped surface argument reliably justify the geometric black-hole production cross section σ ∼ πRSchw(E)² in transplanckian particle collisions when collision-induced curvature and higher-curvature corrections are considered?

Can dissipation during inflation satisfy slow-roll and density-perturbation requirements with mφ≫H, η≫1 and sub-Planckian inflaton amplitudes, thereby avoiding the usual eta problem without symmetry protection of an exceptionally flat potential?

Can coupled supersymmetric flat-direction scalars account for dark matter and present dark energy, attain suitable initial conditions after inflation, and terminate accelerated expansion in the future?

Can a discrete gauge symmetry protect the axion's accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against gravitational violations, while supersymmetric DFSZ dynamics relates the PQ scale to supersymmetry breaking and generates an electroweak-scale μ parameter?
Can a dimension-six Higgs interaction with a low cutoff produce a strong first-order electroweak transition, satisfy precision constraints, and yield experimentally testable Higgs self-couplings?

How can discrete gauge symmetries protect otherwise vulnerable low-energy selection rules and address baryon violation, R-parity, neutrino masses, the supersymmetric μ problem, flavor hierarchies, and axion stability?
Can natural inflation obtain a sufficiently flat axion potential and an effectively super-Planckian axion scale while keeping the underlying axion scales sub-Planckian?
